posts.hook: I just built Rift Code inside my own OS.
posts.body:
Took 4 hours. Paste any GitHub repo → interactive whiteboard of the code.

Nodes. Edges. Drag. Zoom. Pan.

My 19 agents are the demo. Your repo could be next.

posts.hook: The whiteboard took 4 files to build.
posts.body:
1. GitHub API route (fetches repo tree)
2. React Flow canvas (the whiteboard)
3. Static arsenal graph (19 agents)
4. URL input → visualize any repo

No magic. Just wiring.

posts.hook: 315 points. 19 agents. 0 shelf-ware.
posts.body:
The Superagent Challenge said 200 points wins.

I flooded it with 315.

Stunt Protocol (70) + 18 agents + orchestrator. Every one runs daily.

posts.body:

posts.hook: Most agency tools are single-purpose.
posts.body:
One tool for scheduling.
One for analytics.
One for content.
One for finance.

I built 19 inside one operating system.

The whiteboard visualizes all of them. In one view.

posts.hook: Another chat ran out of credits mid-build.
posts.body:
I had a fully-built Stunt Protocol Engine (70 pts) sitting UNCOMMITTED in my workspace.

New chat picked it up in 2 minutes:
- Pushed the stranded work
- Built 13 more agents
- Wired them all into an orchestrator
- Shipped a whiteboard visualization feature

That's not 'picking up where we left off.' That's a system.

posts.hook: 275 challenge points, verified live.
posts.body:
python quartermaster.py status
→ [x] 19/19 active

Every agent ran end-to-end. Every one is committed. Every one is pushed.

posts.hook: Why React Flow, not custom SVG.
posts.body:
I had 2 choices for the Whiteboard:

A) Build custom canvas with pan/zoom/drag
B) Use @xyflow/react (standard)

B won. Why? Demo-ready in 2 hours. Controls, minimap, drag, theming out of the box.

For the Superagent Challenge deadline, shipping > purity.

posts.hook: The GitHub API has a 60-req/hr limit.
posts.body:
So I put the fetch on a Next.js server route with 5-minute caching.

No client-side API calls.
No rate-limit drama.
Just works.
